errors.english: then one might not want Jaimini and the others to be the ones who know that object, but rather claim it is through inference
errors.why: The opponent says he does not hold that Jaimini and others know the supersensible object by perception, but by inference; the English makes him deny that Jaimini knows it at all.

note: The Mīmāṃsā/apauruṣeya argument is largely followed, with one muddled rendering of the opponent's reply.

errors.why: rung ba is the technical 'perceptible / fit to be perceived' (dṛśya); the phrase is the non-existence of a perceptible thing, not of 'suitability' (similarly 'It is also not suitable' at the opening).

errors.english: Because the reversal of that (vyapti) pervasion is established as a subversion
errors.why: The sense is that when existence is absent, the absence (vyatireka) of such perception is established; 'subversion' and the pervasion gloss garble the logical point.

note: Dense anupalabdhi argument rendered with recurring misreadings of technical terms and a stray editorial insertion; needs a specialist pass.
Faithful verse rendering of the Jetavana founding episode, with the Sanskrit lines transliterated in a note.

errors.english: even a permanent entity must necessarily produce a distinct state from its cooperative causes
errors.why: The question is why the cooperating factors must necessarily produce a distinction in the permanent entity; the entity is the patient, not the producer.

note: Sound rendering of the argument against permanent causes needing cooperators and the conclusion on causeless destruction.
Faithful verse translation of Bodhicaryāvatāra ch. 9 (mind-only, illusion, wish-fulfilling jewel and Garuḍa pillar, need for emptiness).

errors.english: were greatly displeased [note: with the cycle of birth and death]
errors.why: The note supplies an object the Tibetan does not give; the nāgas' dismay is at their own condition as heard in the story, not stated as saṃsāra in general.

note: Accurate narrative and verses on Saṅgha property; one speculative translator's note.
